sentences.text: Ares -LRB- -LSB- ˈɛəriːz -RSB- Ἄρης -LSB- árɛːs -RSB- -RRB- is the Greek god of war .	Greek god	List of Greek mythological figures	of war	war god
He is one of the Twelve Olympians , and the son of Zeus and Hera .	Zeus	Zeus	Hera	Hera	Twelve Olympians	Twelve Olympians

In Greek literature , he often represents the physical or violent and untamed aspect of war , in contrast to his sister the armored Athena , whose functions as a goddess of intelligence include military strategy and generalship .	Athena	Athena	of war	war god	Greek literature	ancient Greek literature	goddess of intelligence	knowledge deity	military strategy	military strategy	generalship	general officer

The Greeks were ambivalent toward Ares : although he embodied the physical valor necessary for success in war , he was a dangerous force , `` overwhelming , insatiable in battle , destructive , and man-slaughtering . ''	ambivalent	Wiktionary:ambivalent#English

His sons Phobos -LRB- Fear -RRB- and Deimos -LRB- Terror -RRB- and his lover , or sister , Enyo -LRB- Discord -RRB- accompanied him on his war chariot .	chariot	chariot	Enyo	Enyo	Phobos	Phobos (mythology)	Deimos	Deimos (mythology)
In the Iliad , his father Zeus tells him that he is the god most hateful to him .	Zeus	Zeus	Iliad	Iliad
An association with Ares endows places and objects with a savage , dangerous , or militarized quality .

His value as a war god is placed in doubt : during the Trojan War , Ares was on the losing side , while Athena , often depicted in Greek art as holding Nike -LRB- Victory -RRB- in her hand , favoured the triumphant Greeks .	Athena	Athena	Trojan War	Trojan War	Greek art	ancient Greek art

Ares plays a relatively limited role in Greek mythology as represented in literary narratives , though his numerous love affairs and abundant offspring are often alluded to .	Greek mythology	Greek mythology	alluded	allusion
When Ares does appear in myths , he typically faces humiliation .
He is well known as the lover of Aphrodite , the goddess of love , who was married to Hephaestus , god of craftsmanship .	Aphrodite	Aphrodite	Hephaestus	Hephaestus
The most famous story related to Ares and Aphrodite shows them exposed to ridicule through the wronged husband 's device .	Aphrodite	Aphrodite

The counterpart of Ares among the Roman gods is Mars , who as a father of the Roman people was given a more important and dignified place in ancient Roman religion as a guardian deity .	Mars	Mars (mythology)	Roman gods	List of Roman deities	ancient Roman religion	Religion in ancient Rome	guardian deity	tutelary deity

During the Hellenization of Latin literature , the myths of Ares were reinterpreted by Roman writers under the name of Mars .	Mars	Mars (mythology)	Hellenization	Hellenization	Latin literature	Latin literature	reinterpreted	interpretatio graeca

Greek writers under Roman rule also recorded cult practices and beliefs pertaining to Mars under the name of Ares .	Mars	Mars (mythology)	Roman rule	Roman Empire	cult practices	cult (religious practice)

Thus in the classical tradition of later Western art and literature , the mythology of the two figures becomes virtually indistinguishable .	classical tradition	classical mythology	Western art and literature	Western culture
